Subject: Recap + next steps from today's discovery: performance targets and benchmarking

Alex / Priya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of the performance items we covered and proposed next steps so we're aligned before exchanging the benchmark artifacts:

Key targets you mentioned on the call:
- Latency: p50 target ~120ms, p95 target ~350ms (end-to-end, streaming-enabled for partial token emission)
- Throughput: sustained 200 req/s with burst capacity up to 600 req/s for short windows
- Concurrency: typical concurrency ~8 concurrent requests per model instance, peak up to 32 during scans
- Streaming: partial token streaming is required for the low-latency UX (client expects first token within 80–100ms ideally)

Next steps we agreed:
1) Redwood will share our benchmark harness + prompt set and a clear measurement definition document (this will include cold vs warm cache runs, replayed production traffic, and reproducibility notes).
2) EdgeFin will confirm final SLO windows and provide a production traffic sample (anonymized) for replay.
3) We'll run a preliminary set of runs on a Redwood Dedicated pool or provide scripts so EdgeFin can run locally — TBD which is preferred.
4) Follow-up meeting: propose Mar 2, 10:00 AM PT to review results and iterate on methodology.

Attached: placeholder attachments we'll push to Drive: redwood-benchmark-harness-v1.zip, edgefin-promptset-v2.csv, s3-benchmark-scripts.sh

Questions for you now: which option do you want (Redwood-run vs EdgeFin-run)? Also confirm whether the replayed traffic should simulate KV cache warm state or include cold-start windows.

Thanks — Marissa

Marissa — great summary, thanks. Quick clarifications from our side so the harness and measurement definitions match what we'll need to sign off on an SLA:

- Latency definitions: p50/p95 should be measured at token-emission time during streaming and include end-to-end client->model->client network time (so you can capture serialization/deserialization overhead). For long responses (1k tokens), we'd like percentile breakdowns by token window (first 1 token, first 16 tokens, full response completion).
- Throughput: sustained 200 req/s is the baseline; during market opens we expect short bursts up to 600 req/s for ~30–60s. Please ensure the harness can replay burst patterns versus steady-state.
- Concurrency: each simulated user may open 1 streaming connection with multiple in-flight token windows; treat concurrency as active request handles rather than socket count.
- Reproducibility: provide a deterministic prompt set with seeded randomness and a way to pin model version + quantization profile.

We prefer Redwood to run the first pass (so we can get a neutral baseline), then we'll run the same harness in our environment. Can you share the harness and a README for reproducing?

I'll attach our sample anonymized traffic (will send via secure link) — Priya will follow up with that.

Thanks — Alex

Alex — attaching the initial harness we discussed and a concise measurement-definition doc below (attachments uploaded to the Drive link in the thread). High level notes:

Attached artifacts (zip contains scripts and a k8s manifest for cluster-based runs):
- redwood-benchmark-harness-v1.zip (harness, runner scripts, example k6 + Python runner)
- edgefin-promptset-v2.csv (anonymized prompts + expected token lengths + categories)
- s3-benchmark-scripts.sh (helper to upload logs to S3 after runs)

Measurement definitions (summary):
- Latency: measure at two points — (A) first-byte (first token emitted) and (B) response-complete. Report p50/p90/p95/p99 for both. For streaming runs, capture per-token latency distribution and a derived metric for "time to first token".
- Throughput: measured as completed requests per second (RPS) observed at the client since streaming can make RPS ambiguous; report both offered load (requests/sec sent by the harness) and completed RPS.
- Concurrency: number of active request handles (streaming sessions) during measurement windows.
- Cold vs warm: cold-run = fresh model instance with empty KV cache + cold jit cache, warm-run = warmed model process and warmed KV caches. We will surface both as separate result sets.
- Reproducibility: harness seeds all randomness where possible; scripts pin model artifact SHA, quantization flags, and kernel selection. Include run metadata (docker image ids, commit SHAs) with logs.

Repro steps we recommend for EdgeFin-run (if you run locally):
1) Pull harness repo and pin to tag v1.0.0.
2) Start 3 warmup runs to prime caches.
3) Run 3 steady-state runs (5 minutes each) at the target sustained throughput (200 RPS), capture full logs.
4) Run 3 burst-window runs (simulate 600 RPS for 30s), capture metrics.
5) Upload logs to the shared Drive / S3 bucket and send link.

I'll upload the full zip and prompt set to the Drive folder and share edit access with Alex + Priya. Let me know if you want us to run on Redwood Dedicated and share the raw logs versus you running locally.

Best — Marissa

Alex / Marissa — a few technical details we should call out so the numbers are apples-to-apples:

1) Cache semantics: we need to be explicit about KV cache state and batching. For streaming, KV cache hits change emission latency significantly — so a warm-run must include the same prompt distribution as production traffic to simulate realistic cache hit rates.
2) Model variants: if you test quantized vs fp16 we must pin and report the kernel/runtime flags. Different quantization yields different CPU/GPU kernel paths — we'll include a table in the run metadata.
3) Network places to measure: client-side measurement vs server-side measurement can differ by ~10–30ms depending on serialization. We'll collect both and publish a delta.
4) Reproducibility artifacts: include the harness PID logs, worker thread counts, and seed files. The harness currently includes a --seed flag and a run-metadata.json (with image tags) in the zip.

Can you confirm the target model size (e.g., 13B vs 70B) we should pin in the manifest and whether you want us to exercise both? Also confirm if you need the streaming-first-token SLA to be measured on an edge proxy vs direct host (proxy adds overhead).

Thanks — Dylan
